title: Kung Fu Theater
blurb: Saturday afternoon on a UHF channel: Hong Kong kung fu and the ninja boom of the 80s. Dubbed badly, fought brilliantly.

films.note: Yuen Woo-ping directs Yuen Biao as a cowardly laundryman who has to fight a killer. The lion dance alone is worth it.
The one the Wu-Tang Clan named a song after. A student learns to fight like he plays chess.
Angela Mao, Golden Harvest's fiercest fighter, taking on a gang single-handed.
Sam Hui as a brainwashed assassin, from the manga that became Crying Freeman.
The film that started America's ninja craze.
Early Tsui Hark: a kung fu comedy set in a village of cannibals.
Sho Kosugi takes the lead, and Salt Lake City gets a ninja war.
An aerobics instructor is possessed by a ninja's spirit. That is the plot.
Blaxploitation meets kung fu, shot in Manila by Cirio Santiago.
Godfrey Ho's cut-and-paste ninja film. Golden ninja figurines, a pink ninja suit, and no sense at all.
Bruceploitation at its most shameless. The poster promises far more than the film delivers.
Three killers made into martial arts weapons by a mad scientist. Made in LA, cheaply.
Swordplay, flying leaps and a stolen treasure, dubbed with total confidence.
Bruce Lee's tournament on a private island, and the hall of mirrors everyone copies.
Gordon Liu earns his way through thirty-five chambers of Shaolin training. The training montage movie.
The Shaw Brothers film that started the American craze in 1973. Watch for the glowing hands.
Jackie Chan's breakout as a young Wong Fei-hung who fights best drunk.
A blind assassin with a hat that takes heads, at a tournament of every style there is.
Sonny Chiba at his most brutal. The first film rated X in America for violence alone.
Jackie Chan invents the cat's claw by watching a cat fight a snake.
The Venom Mob again: four men maimed by a warlord learn to fight around what he took.
Chang Cheh's ninjas come in gold, wood, water, fire and earth, and each one is ridiculous.
Hammer and the Shaw Brothers together: Peter Cushing and seven kung fu siblings against Dracula.
Sammo Hung fights ghosts, a sorcerer and his own nerves. The film that started the kung fu ghost comedy.
Villains named Iron Robe and Golden Arm, each with a metal superpower.
Tsui Hark throws every effect he can find at a war between heaven and earth.
Lau Kar-leung's comedy of fights disguised as tea tasting and antique appraisal.
Hung Hsi-kuan against the White Brows priest, whose weak spot moves around his body.
A marriage quarrel over whose martial arts are better turns into China against Japan.
Lau Kar-leung plays a broken monkey-style master who teaches a street kid everything.
Yuen Biao learns Wing Chun from Sammo Hung after finding out every fight he won was bought.
Shaw Brothers horror: two rival masters and a lantern maker working in human skin.
Cheap, silly and undead: a hopping corpse gets a kung fu rematch.
The last kung fu masters against guns, voodoo and each other.
A prison brawler who punches through people. Gloriously, absurdly gory.
Jim Kelly, after Enter the Dragon, defends a karate school in Los Angeles.
Etsuko Shihomi takes on a new henchman with a new style every ten minutes.
Ninjas burst out of the ground, the sea and each other. Ching Siu-tung's first film.
Motown kung fu in Harlem: Bruce Leroy looks for the glow.
A Shaolin master hides from the Qing with an orphan who wants to learn.
